title: PRESSER | Chris Beard - Maui Preview (11-19-26)
text: So, with the Maui Invitational coming up, what type of opportunity do you think this presents for your team? >> Yeah, I think it's big uh not only for our team, but really for our brand and our program. It's the first time that uh Old Miss has been in the Maui Classic. Um you know, it's it's one of or if not still the best basketball tournament, you know, in basketball. This thing's been around since the 80s. So, um all sorts of unique things about this, you know, like the teams that have success in this tournament over the years. it's related directly to NCA tournament experience and and success. And so, um, I think it's big for this year's team. It's an opportunity. We're looking forward to it. But also think as we continue to build the program to put the Old Miss brand in these type situations is why we came to Oxford >> for this team. Is there anything from the Puerto Rico trip that you can draw on to take with you? >> Yeah, great question. So, this a unique uh tournament. We got three games in three days, right? And so, reminding our players this morning in practice that we've been in this situation before. First of all, we've had multiple uh three-day periods uh since we came together as a team this summer where we have three back-to-back practices. We've had days where we had back-to-back inter squad scrimmages and then certainly in Puerto Rico, you know, we chose in Puerto Rico to play backto backs. A lot of teams around the country that do the uh international tours, we'll play a game, take a couple days off, play another game. We we specifically chose to play backtoback in Puerto Rico knowing that this year's schedule had the Maui. The team has been very dominant in the first couple games, you know, against these low major programs. What do you think's the biggest adjustment, you know, playing against high major teams in the Maui? >> Yeah, I think twofold. I think, you know, we tell the guys all all the time, we is more important than anybody we play. We spend the majority of our practice time, film study time, really mental space thinking about our team, the things that we have to improve. Uh then certainly when it comes to game prep, you know, you get ready for the opponent. So I think uh you know the question relative to kind of the teams we played on our schedule to this point they were on the schedule that's the opportunity we have but we all understand now we're getting into more of a power force setting. So I think most important is we because some of the things we've done early season translate to this level of competition. Um then the scouting is real as well. >> What is the scout on Clemson now that Nichols is in the rear view? >> Yeah I think Clemson obviously uh a storied program a lot of tradition three straight NCA tournaments. Uh Brad is one of the longest tenure coaches in power four. He's been there well over 15 years. And so we know what we're getting into. We're getting into a program that expects to win. Um this year's team's a really good team. They have returners uh that were part of their NCA tournament team last year. They've added really um talented guys from the portal and got a couple young guys help them as well. Brad's team always have a um an identity. We know defensively they're going to be uh gritty, patient, tough to score against. Do a great job with size. I think they're one of the tallest teams in the country, if that makes sense. And then on offense, kind of a dual threat. They put a lot of pressure on the rim with back cuts and screening. And they're obviously a three-point shooting team as well. >> You know, we're expecting more competitive matchups in the Maui. How do you all plan to, you know, manage the rotation and the uh the minute allocations to all the players? >> Yeah, I think a couple things. You know, three games in three days. I think depth has to be a part of any team that's a contender in this tournament. Um we feel like depth could help us in this tournament. You know, we've got 10 12 deep where we can play guys. Um in terms of rotations, we're, you know, early season still. We're work in progress. Um I know this, we told the guys this morning, everybody that gets on that plane tomorrow morning is ready to play. You know, you never know when your opportunity is going to come. >> We'll talk to him later today, but how have you seen Ben evolve in his first college games coming from Australia? >> Yeah, I think the biggest positive with Ben so far is we seem to see him getting more comfortable. Uh Ben's an alpha. He's a competitive guy. I think last game some of his playmaking ability with his passing and those are things we see all the time in practice. But I think as uh Ben continues to get comfortable uh the adjustments that he's are fighting are really just pro basketball to college basketball spacing level of athleticism on the floor. Um I think the biggest positive we have with Ben right now is he seems to be getting more comfortable playing college basketball. >> First in the nation scoring defense and also turnover margin. What can you say about your team's defensive efforts so far? Yeah, those two things are by design. I think it's too early in the season to really looking at the stats, but uh that's where we want it to be. The question is because can we sustain it? Um so points allowed is an important thing around here. We want to be a team that's tough to score against and certainly this year's uh defensive I think we we've shown the ability with our athleticism uh and our experience to be a team that, you know, tries to turn the opponent over. Um tell the guys almost on a daily basis, defense isn't guarding a guy once he has the ball. You know, defense is trying to go get the ball. >> Thanks, coach. Appreciate you.
